prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1380; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a side impact at a signalized intersection; the claimant reports a wrist fracture and has retained counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is listed on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of loss; no coverage questions remain open at this stage.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision and describes the impact as a side-on hit from the other vehicle's path.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photos and two independent witness statements; both describe the accident the same way the claimant and the other driver have, with no conflicting details noted.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection shows damage to the driver-side door and quarter panel that lines up with the reported point of impact; no prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the appraiser's findings.

Entry 6: Claimant's account has stayed consistent across the recorded call, the written statement, and the follow-up interview through counsel.

Entry 7: Medical records show a wrist fracture consistent in type and force with a side impact of this kind, and the physician's notes support the mechanism described.

Entry 8: Records also show treatment for the same wrist area within the past two years; the attending physician indicates that earlier condition contributes to some of the current complaints, and I am noting it for the file.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course: immobilization, a follow-up procedure, then physical therapy, with the care tapering as the claimant's range of motion improved.

Entry 10: Nothing in the file suggests damage predating the policy's effective date; the vehicle history and prior claims search came back clean.

Entry 11: Sent the attorney the medical authorization forms and requested the complete treatment ledger, including the prior wrist records, to finish the evaluation.

Entry 12: Current evaluation: the injury and vehicle damage fit the reported collision, and the open items are the final bills and the prior-condition apportionment, which I will handle with the medical reviewer.
